---
title: "PBS: Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme"
description: "Information about medicines provided to people under the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme."

Information about medicines provided to people under the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme.

*Explains the medicine subsidy program and links to listings, statistics and supporting information.*

The field it replaces is defined by AIHW METEOR as \"A sequence of alphanumeric, numeric and alphabetic characters which uniquely identify a pharmacy\", a six-character identifier whose first character marks hospital pharmacies and dispensing doctors and whose second gives the state for hospitals. Scrambling removes that structure, so PHRMCY_APPRVL_TYP_CD and PHRMCY_PSTCD carry what is left of it.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 600674, Pharmacy—pharmacy identifier, identifier XXNNNA, which is the unscrambled field this column is derived from","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/600674","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Supplying pharmacy id - scrambled","k":"open_identifier_domain","def":"An opaque key with no readable internal structure, consistent within the collection so that rows sharing a value were dispensed by the same approved supplier.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR 600674, Pharmacy—pharmacy identifier, identifier XXNNNA (Department of Health)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/600674","lim":"The pharmacy type and the state encoded in the real identifier cannot be recovered from it, and it joins to no pharmacy register, so nothing about ownership, banner group, opening hours or accreditation is available. The PBS specification says of the matching pharmacy items that \"In the context of PBS data, this data element describes the location (physical address) of the dispensing pharmacy\", and that the pharmacy's published remoteness category \"is based on the postcode of the pharmacy at which the prescription was dispensed\", which is the postcode held here. Read against PTNT_PSTCD it shows whether a person filled the script near home, and against PRSCRBR_MJR_PSTCD whether they filled it near the prescriber. PHRMCY_ID_SCRAM says which pharmacy; this column says where it is.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the pharmacy location and remoteness items","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Pharmacy postcode","k":"Australian postcode","def":"A four-digit Australian postcode. METeOR's general Australian postcode domain (data element 611398) takes its values from the Postcode datafile and reserves 0097, 0098 and 0099 for not applicable, unknown and not stated, though the PBS specification does not say which of those the extract uses.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the pharmacy location and remoteness items","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","lim":"A postcode is a postal delivery area, so it does not nest inside the ABS statistical areas and any conversion to SA2 or to remoteness runs through a correspondence that carries error. The value also belongs to the claiming approved supplier, which for a hospital pharmacy or a mail-order dispensary can sit a long way from where the patient collected the medicine, so the distance between this postcode and the patient's is a weak proxy for how far anyone travelled.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PRSCRB_DT","d":"The day the prescriber signed the script that this supply was made against.","full":"The day the prescriber signed the script that this supply was made against. METeOR defines it as \"the date on which the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescriber signs the prescription, expressed as DDMMYYYY\", and notes it is \"Not required for continued dispensing\". Subtracting it from SPPLY_DT gives the delay between a medicine being written and being collected, which is the main use of the column. On a repeat supply the date still belongs to the original script, so one prescribing date recurs across all the rows that share a prescription.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 602772, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—date of prescribing, DDMMYYYY' (Department of Health)","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602772","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Date of prescribing","k":"date","def":"A date, published by METeOR in DDMMYYYY form with a maximum of eight characters. It falls on or before the supply date, and can fall well before it where a patient collected a repeat months later.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data element 602772, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—date of prescribing, DDMMYYYY' (Department of Health)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602772","lim":"It is not the date of a consultation and is not evidence the patient saw the prescriber that day, since PBS holds no consultation record and a script can be written without a face-to-face visit; MBS is where an attendance would appear. Because METeOR exempts continued dispensing supplies from reporting it, a missing value can mark a pharmacist supply made without a prescription rather than a data fault.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PRSCRBR_ID_SCRAM","d":"A scrambled key for the prescriber who wrote the prescription, used to group prescribing to one practitioner.","full":"A scrambled key for the prescriber who wrote the prescription, used to group prescribing to one practitioner. AIHW METEOR defines the field it replaces as \"A unique numeric identifier for the prescriber of the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item for which the PBS benefit is being claimed\", and notes that the real identifier may need suppression because it identifies individual prescribers. MJR_SPCLTY_GRP_CD and PRSCRBR_TYP_CD are the only attributes of the prescriber that survive alongside it.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 600762, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—prescriber identifier, identifier N[N(19)], which is the unscrambled field this column is derived from","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/600762","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Prescriber id - scrambled","k":"open_identifier_domain","def":"An opaque key replacing a numeric prescriber number, consistent within the collection so that rows sharing a value were written by the same prescriber.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR 600762, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—prescriber identifier, identifier N[N(19)] (Department of Health)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/600762","lim":"It is not the Medicare provider key, so a doctor's prescribing cannot be joined to their MBS billing in SCRAM_SPR, and a practitioner who holds more than one prescriber number appears as more than one key. Hospital prescriptions are frequently written under a departmental or registrar number, so a high-volume key can be a ward rather than a person.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PRSCRBR_MJR_PSTCD","d":"Where the prescriber did most of their Medicare work, not where this prescription was written.","full":"Where the prescriber did most of their Medicare work, not where this prescription was written. The PBS specification is explicit that the prescriber's location \"is based on the postcode of the location at which the prescriber performed the majority of Medicare services for the most recent relevant quarter\", which is what the MJR token in the name records. It is therefore a property of the doctor over a quarter rather than of the prescribing event on the row. PRSCRBR_ID_SCRAM says which prescriber wrote the script, and PRSCRBR_TYP_CD and MJR_SPCLTY_GRP_CD say what kind of practitioner they are.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the prescriber location and remoteness items","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Prescriber postcode","k":"Australian postcode","def":"A four-digit Australian postcode from the same domain as the patient and pharmacy postcodes on the row, with values drawn from the Postcode datafile behind METeOR data element 611398.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the prescriber location and remoteness items","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","lim":"It cannot place a prescription geographically. A specialist who consults one day a week in a regional town but bills most of their services in a capital city carries the capital's postcode on every script they write, so counts of prescribing by area understate practice in small centres. The quarterly basis also means the value can shift between one patient's rows without the prescriber having moved.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PRSCRBR_TYP_CD","d":"The profession of the person who wrote the prescription: medical practitioner, dentist, optometrist, nurse practitioner or midwife.","full":"The profession of the person who wrote the prescription: medical practitioner, dentist, optometrist, nurse practitioner or midwife. AIHW METEOR defines it as \"The broad field of specialty of the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescriber responsible for the writing and signing of the prescription, as represented by a code\". The available codes are a history of prescribing rights, since optometrists were authorised from 1 January 2008 and nurse practitioners and midwives from 1 September 2010.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 603862, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—prescriber type, code A","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603862","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Prescriber type","k":"pbs_prescriber_type","def":"A single letter with six values: M medical practitioner, D dental practitioner, O optometrist, N nurse practitioner, W midwife, and B for prescribers qualified as both medical and dental practitioners, which appears only in records before 1 January 2008.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR 603862, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—prescriber type, code A (Department of Health)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603862","lim":"The absence of a code before its start date is a rule about authorisation, not evidence about practice, so no nurse practitioner rows exist before September 2010. METeOR defines it as \"the total number of times that the prescribed medicinal product is supplied to the patient or PBS consumer\", and sets the rule that a repeat prescription takes \"a value of 1 for those prescriptions where Regulation 24 applicable indicator has a negative response, or a value equivalent to 1 plus the number of repeats specified by the prescriber\" where that indicator is positive. It rises above 1 only on the Regulation 24 rows, where the original and all its repeats went out together. Counting rows counts supply events; summing this column counts the supplies bundled inside them.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 605072, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised medication supplies, total number N[N]' (Department of Health)","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/605072","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Number of authorised medication supplies","k":"count of supplies","def":"A whole number in METeOR's format N[N], two characters at most, with 99 reserved for not stated or inadequately described. Ordinary rows carry 1, and a Regulation 24 row carries 1 plus the repeats the prescriber allowed, so a script with five repeats supplied at once carries 6.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data element 605072, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised medication supplies, total number N[N]' (Department of Health)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/605072","lim":"It is not a count of prescriptions written and not a count of packs, so summing it over a patient's year gives supply occasions rather than scripts or medicines held. AIHW METEOR defines it as \"For a given prescription, the total number of times that the prescribed medicinal product has previously been supplied to the patient or Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) consumer, including the original supply\". A single-supply prescription records 1, and a repeat prescription counts up as each repeat is dispensed, so this column tells you where in a prescription's life the row sits, while RPT_ORDR_NMBR says how many repeats were allowed.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 603916, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of times previously supplied, total number N[N]","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603916","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Number of times previously supplied","k":"count_with_not_stated","def":"One or two digits, format N[N]: 1 on an original supply, rising with each subsequent supply up to 98, and 99 reserved for not stated or inadequately described.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR 603916, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of times previously supplied, total number N[N] (Department of Health)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603916","lim":"The count belongs to one prescription form, not to a course of treatment. A fresh prescription resets it to 1, so it cannot measure how long someone has been taking a medicine or whether they persisted with it. The 99 code is missing data rather than a large count, and averaging the column without excluding it will pull any mean sharply upwards.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PTNT_BRTH_MTH","d":"The calendar month of the patient's birth, held without a day so no row can be dated to a birthday.","full":"The calendar month of the patient's birth, held without a day so no row can be dated to a birthday. The PBS specification says the underlying field is the patient's date of birth and that \"'Patient date of birth' is extracted from the Medicare record of the patient, as reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS)\", which PLIDA splits into this column and PTNT_BRTH_YR. Taken with the year it fixes age at supply to within a month, which is what age-group analyses of dispensing rest on. It describes the person the medicine was supplied to, not the prescriber and not whoever paid.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Month of birth","k":"month of year, 1 to 12","def":"A month number from 1 to 12, carrying the month component of METeOR's date of birth element (287007), whose full domain is DDMMYYYY. The day component is not supplied in this asset.","p":"2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","lim":"On its own it gives no age, cannot order two people's births inside a month, and cannot be joined to a full date of birth held in another dataset. It also inherits whatever the Medicare enrolment holds, so a birth date estimated at enrolment leaves a month that is administrative rather than real, and there is no accuracy flag on the row to show which values those are.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 160 more"]},{"n":"PTNT_BRTH_YR","d":"The calendar year of the patient's birth, the coarser half of the birth date PLIDA keeps for PBS.","full":"The calendar year of the patient's birth, the coarser half of the birth date PLIDA keeps for PBS. The PBS specification says of the underlying field that it \"can be used to identify individual patients and may, in some use cases, need to be suppressed or perturbed\", which is why only a year and a month survive here, and that it \"is extracted from the Medicare record of the patient, as reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS)\". Subtracting it from the year of SPPLY_DT gives age at supply to within a year, and PTNT_BRTH_MTH tightens that to a month. It is the patient's year of birth, not the year they came onto Medicare.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Year of birth","k":"calendar year","def":"A four-digit calendar year, the year component of METeOR's DDMMYYYY date of birth element (287007). Values run from the birth year of the oldest enrolled Medicare patient up to the year of the extract.","p":"2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","lim":"It cannot settle whether a patient had passed an age threshold on the day of supply, which matters for concession rules and for paediatric dosing, because the day of birth is gone. A year here also cannot be assumed to agree with the year of birth in Census, birth or death records: each comes from a separate enrolment or form, and the spine links people rather than reconciling the dates they reported.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 160 more"]},{"n":"PTNT_CNTRBTN_AMT","d":"What the patient paid the pharmacy for this supply, on the PBS's narrow definition of a co-payment.","full":"What the patient paid the pharmacy for this supply, on the PBS's narrow definition of a co-payment. METeOR defines it as \"the total amount paid by the patient or PBS consumer to the approved pharmacy for a prescription, exclusive of any special patient contributions, e.g. brand price premiums or therapeutic group premiums\", and adds that the amount \"also excludes any optional fees imposed at the discretion of the pharmacy and payable by the patient\". The value moves with the patient's entitlement rather than with the medicine, so it is set by PTNT_CTGRY_DRVD_CD and by whether the Safety Net threshold had been reached that calendar year. With BNFT_AMT it splits the dispensed price between the patient and the Commonwealth.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 603362, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—PBS patient contribution, total Australian currency N[NNNNN].NN' (Department of Health)","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603362","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Patient contribution amount","k":"Australian currency amount, dollars and cents","def":"Australian currency to two decimal places, in METeOR's format N[NNNNN].NN. The value tracks the co-payment published in the Schedule of Pharmaceutical Benefits, which METeOR says is adjusted each 1 January in line with the CPI, although statute has since frozen the concessional rate at $7.70 for 2025 to 2029: METeOR gives $36.90 for a general patient and $6.00 for a concessional patient in 2014, and the schedule's fee table gave $25.00 and $7.70 as at 1 July 2026.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data element 603362, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—PBS patient contribution, total Australian currency N[NNNNN].NN' (Department of Health)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603362","lim":"It is not the money that left the patient's pocket. Brand price premiums, therapeutic group premiums and any discretionary pharmacy fee are excluded by definition, so a patient who chose a premium brand paid more than this column shows. It is also not a basis for a consistent affordability series over the whole 2006 to 2025 span, because supplies priced below the general co-payment were not collected at all until April 2012.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PTNT_CTGRY_DRVD_CD","d":"The patient's PBS entitlement at the moment of supply: general or concessional, and whether the Safety Net had been reached.","full":"The patient's PBS entitlement at the moment of supply: general or concessional, and whether the Safety Net had been reached. AIHW METEOR defines it as \"The derived entitlement status of the patient at the time the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item is supplied, as represented by a code\", derived by combining payment category with patient payment category. It determines what appears in PTNT_CNTRBTN_AMT and BNFT_AMT on the same row, so it is the field that explains why two supplies of the same item cost different amounts.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 604103, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—patient entitlement status (derived), Commonwealth government assistance scheme code AX","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/604103","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Patient entitlement status (derived)","k":"pbs_patient_entitlement_status_derived","def":"Two characters, format AX. Someone who gains or loses a concession card changes code part-way through a year, and Safety Net status resets every calendar year and returns as the year's prescriptions accumulate, so the column measures entitlement on the day and cannot stand in for a stable indicator of low income.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PTNT_PSTCD","d":"The postal area of the patient's home as Medicare last recorded it, which is not necessarily where they lived when the medicine was supplied.","full":"The postal area of the patient's home as Medicare last recorded it, which is not necessarily where they lived when the medicine was supplied. The PBS specification says the derived patient state \"is derived from 'Patient postcode', i.e. it is derived from the Medicare record of the patient and is based on the most recent patient address reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS)\", and this column is that postcode. It is the geography every patient-side analysis of PBS rests on, including the remoteness categories the department publishes. Set against PHRMCY_PSTCD it shows whether the script was filled near home.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient state item","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Patient postcode","k":"Australian postcode","def":"A four-digit Australian postcode. METeOR's general Australian postcode domain (data element 611398) sources values from the Postcode datafile and reserves 0097, 0098 and 0099 for not applicable, unknown and not stated.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient state item","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","lim":"Medicare holds one current address rather than an address history, so an old value can be stamped on a recent supply and a move stays invisible until the person tells Services Australia. The postcode also belongs to an enrolment rather than to a residence: a child on a parent's record carries the parent's postcode, and someone living away for study or care may carry a family address. For an actual residential history the address episodes in Core Locations, keyed by ARID, are the source.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PTNT_SEX_CD","d":"The patient's sex as the Medicare entitlement record held it at the moment the claim was archived.","full":"The patient's sex as the Medicare entitlement record held it at the moment the claim was archived. METeOR's PBS note is explicit that \"this data item is defined as being 'the gender of the consumer as held in the entitlement tables at the time the PBS claim was archived'\", and warns that \"gender is a social/cultural concept rather than a biological (anatomical or chromosomal) concept, although for most people the two concepts are the same\". It belongs to the patient the medicine was supplied to, not to the prescriber or the cardholder. With PTNT_BRTH_YR it gives the two demographic splits available on a PBS row without leaving the table.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 602450, 'Person—sex, code A' (Department of Health), with the PBS specific note recorded against it","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602450","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Patient sex","k":"sex code","def":"A one-character alphabetic code from METeOR's Sex code A domain, covering male, female, and intersex or indeterminate, with separate supplementary codes for not stated or inadequately described and for unknown, and a blank also read as unknown.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data element 602450, 'Person—sex, code A' (Department of Health), with the PBS specific note recorded against it","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602450","lim":"It is a point-in-time administrative value, so a person whose Medicare record changed will carry different codes on rows before and after the change and a person-level mode will quietly erase that. It is also not comparable with the sex and gender items in Census, surveys or birth records, which are self-reported against different questions, so a disagreement between PBS and Census is not by itself evidence of a bad link.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"RGLTN24_IND","d":"Whether the pharmacist was allowed to hand over the original script and all its repeats at once.","full":"Whether the pharmacist was allowed to hand over the original script and all its repeats at once. METeOR defines it as \"an indicator of whether supply of the original Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item and all repeats is made at the one time\", under a regulation that \"allows a pharmacist to supply an original prescription medication and all of its repeats at the one time\", and restricts such prescriptions to medical practitioners, midwives and nurse practitioners. Where it is positive, PRSCRPTN_CNT and PBS_RGLTN24_ADJST_QTY on the same row cover the whole bundle instead of a single supply, so this is the switch that decides how those two columns should be read.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 601746, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—Regulation 24 applicable indicator, yes/no code A' (Department of Health)","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/601746","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Regulation 24 applicable indicator","k":"yes/no code","def":"A one-character code with only two permissible values, one for yes and one for no, and no supplementary values published. AIHW METEOR warns that \"the number of repeats specified in a given prescription is typically one less than the total number of times that the patient can be supplied with the prescribed medication\", so five repeats permit six supplies in all. The value can differ from the repeats listed in the PBS Schedule for the item, because the prescriber decides how many to write, and PRVS_SPPLY_NMBR records how far through them a given row is.","dsrc":"AIHW METEOR data element 603919, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised prescription repeats, total number N[N]","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603919","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Number of authorised prescription repeats","k":"count_with_not_stated","def":"One or two digits, format N[N]: 0 for a single-supply prescription, 1 to 98 for the repeats authorised, and 99 for not stated or inadequately described.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR 603919, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised prescription repeats, total number N[N] (Department of Health)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603919","lim":"It records what was authorised, not what the patient collected. METeOR defines it as \"the date on which the prescribed medicinal product is supplied by a pharmacist to the patient or PBS consumer\", and explains that it \"essentially equates to the date of purchase\", usually but not always the same as the dispensing date printed on the label. Prefer it to PRSCRB_DT, which belongs to the script, and to EXTRCT_DT, which belongs to the claim file. Each row is one supply, so a patient's repeats appear as separate rows with separate supply dates unless Regulation 24 applied and they all went out together.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 602767, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—date of supply, DDMMYYYY' (Department of Health)","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602767","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Date of supply","k":"date","def":"A date, published by METeOR in DDMMYYYY form with a maximum of eight characters. METeOR defines the element as \"an indicator of whether a prescription is a repeat prescription or an original prescription, as represented by a code\", and puts the initial supply of a script that allows repeats on the original side, not the repeat side. It is what lets a patient's rows be grouped into prescriptions instead of counted as separate treatment decisions. PRVS_SPPLY_NMBR says how many supplies came earlier in this one and RPT_ORDR_NMBR how many the prescriber authorised.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 604005, 'Prescription—repeat prescription indicator, code X' (Department of Health)","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/604005","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Repeat prescription indicator","k":"repeat prescription code","def":"A one-character code with two published meanings: a blank marks an original prescription, including the first supply of one that allows repeats, and a single letter marks a repeat supply. The PBS Explanatory Notes state that \"prior approval is not required from Services Australia or DVA to prescribe an Authority required (STREAMLINED) item\" and that \"an authority prescription for an Authority required (STREAMLINED) item is not valid unless the code is included on the prescription form\". Each code is published against the item's restriction in the Schedule, so it names the indication the prescriber attested to.","dsrc":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, PBS Explanatory Notes, Section 1.2, Prescribing Medicines — Information for PBS Prescribers","durl":"https://www.pbs.gov.au/info/healthpro/explanatory-notes/section1/Section_1_2_Explanatory_Notes","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Streamlined authority code","k":"pbs_streamlined_authority_code","def":"A four or five digit number identifying one restriction, that is one indication and its clinical criteria, on one listed item. Every PBS row belongs to one person, and this is what lets a dispensing history be assembled from the monthly tables and then joined to that person's MBS services, Centrelink payments, tax records and Census responses. ABS calls the Person Linkage Spine \"central to our data linking methods\" and builds it from the combined population of the Medicare Consumer Directory, DOMINO Centrelink Administrative Data and Personal Income Tax records, so PBS is linked to the Spine once rather than to each dataset in turn. In this package the values are synthetic: they are consistent across tables but stand for nobody.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Linkage Spine","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/about/data-services/data-integration/person-linkage-spine","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Synthetic MADIP Person ID","k":"PLIDA person linkage spine identifier (synthetic)","def":"An opaque identifier with no internal structure, one value per person, stable across the monthly PBS tables and across every other dataset linked through the Spine. There is no finite list to publish: the domain is as large as the Spine population, which ABS says aims to cover everyone resident in Australia at any point in the reference period, currently January 2006 to June 2025.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Person Linkage Spine","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/about/data-services/data-integration/person-linkage-spine","lim":"It identifies a person, not a prescription, a household or a Medicare card, so rows sharing a value are one patient's supplies rather than a family's, and a script filled for a child sits under the child. Under co-payment supplies produce no government benefit, so they are invisible in claims data and were only reported at all after approved suppliers were required to lodge them from 1 April 2012. The companion concept in AIHW METEOR is the PBS claim type, whose code U covers claims where \"the dispensed price of the prescribed medicinal product is less than the amount of the applicable co-payment\".","dsrc":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, PBS Under Co-payment Data, and AIHW METEOR data element 603902, PBS claim type, code A","durl":"https://www.pbs.gov.au/info/statistics/under-co-payment/under-co-payment-data","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Under co-payment prescription type","k":"Short code distinguishing types of under co-payment prescription; null where the claim is not under co-payment (inferred)","def":"A short code separating general from concessional under co-payment supplies, held as 1 and 2, and null on rows that are ordinary co-payment claims. The two code values are inferred from the field's role, since the Department publishes the concept but not this column's internal values.","p":"2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025","s":"guessed","src":"AIHW METeOR 603902, PBS claim type, code A (supports the under co-payment concept and its collection from 1 April 2012, not this field's code list)","lim":"It is empty for everything dispensed before 1 April 2012, so a count of all PBS prescriptions that spans that date shows a jump which is a change in reporting rather than in medicine use. Concessional patients also reach the co-payment threshold at a far lower price than general patients, so the two codes are not comparable measures of how cheap a medicine was.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 160 more"],"dom":1}]}</script>
